pick.name: Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing)
pick.what: Microsoft-managed code-signing with short-lived certificates in HSMs; plugs into SignTool, GitHub Actions
pick.why: Managed public-trust signing with no hardware token, about $9.99/month (cheaper than a $150-300/yr OV cert), CI-friendly; SmartScreen reputation still builds over time
pick.free_limits: Needs a paid Azure subscription. Basic $9.99/month incl. 5,000 signatures; Premium $99.99/month incl. 100,000; overage $0.005 per signature (Azure Retail Prices API, US list price).

best_free.name: Microsoft Store (MSIX; Store signs the package)
best_free.what: Submit MSIX; Microsoft signs after certification; winget can point users to it
best_free.why: The only $0, worldwide route with no SmartScreen warnings: Microsoft re-signs MSIX packages after Store certification
best_free.free_limits: Store re-signs MSIX for free; MSI/EXE submitted to the Store and any direct downloads still need your own Authenticode certificate. Developer account registration is free (storedeveloper.microsoft.com).

alts.name: OV code-signing certificate (Sectigo/DigiCert/SSL.com/Certum) on HSM/cloud signing
alts.why: Needed for direct EXE/NSIS downloads without warnings building over time
alts.free_limits: Paid, typically $150-300/yr (Microsoft guidance). CA/B Forum rules since June 2023 require HSM or hardware-token key storage. EV ($400+/yr) no longer bypasses SmartScreen.

alts.name: SignPath Foundation
alts.what: Free signing for genuine OSS projects
alts.free_limits: OSI licence, no proprietary components or dual-licensing

candidates.name: Azure Artifact Signing
candidates.verdict: Pick where eligible; no EV certs

candidates.name: OV/EV certificate from a CA (Sectigo, DigiCert, SSL.com, Certum)
candidates.verdict: Works everywhere; costs and HSM handling

candidates.name: SignPath Foundation
candidates.verdict: Free for OSI-licensed open source only

decision: Azure Artifact Signing is the best overall managed option wherever the founder or company is eligible. Elsewhere, or for free, ship through the Microsoft Store as MSIX; buy a CA-issued OV certificate only when buyers require a directly downloaded installer.
details: Eligibility: organizations in US, Canada, EU, UK, Australia, NZ, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Israel; individuals US/Canada only. Not available on free/trial Azure subscriptions.

region_notes.US: Individual developers and organizations are eligible for Artifact Signing public-trust certificates.
region_notes.EU: Organizations in EU countries, Switzerland and Norway are eligible; individuals are not.
region_notes.UK: Organizations are eligible; individual developers are not (individuals only US/Canada).
region_notes.India: India is not in the eligible country list (quickstart, opened); use Microsoft Store MSIX, a CA-issued OV certificate, or a company formed in an eligible country.

os_notes.Windows: Sign with SignTool/dlib, GitHub Action or Azure DevOps task.
os_notes.macOS: Signing from macOS is not covered by the docs read; use a Windows CI runner.
os_notes.Linux: Same; use a Windows runner or a CA cloud-signing API.

verify.note: Price resolved: Retail Prices API lists 'Trusted Signing' Basic Account $9.99/month, Premium Account $99.99/month, Signature Overage $0.005; Microsoft's code-signing-options page also says ~$9.99/month. Eligibility in notes matches the quickstart (updated 2026-10-08): organizations in US, Canada, EU, UK, Australia, NZ, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Israel; individuals US/Canada only; India not listed. Note the older code-signing-options page (2026-08-29) still lists only US/CA/EU/UK for organizations.
